inputs.original_text: South Dakota Governor Larry Rhoden signed Senate Bill 175 on Thursday, imposing a new requirement that fresh voter registrants must prove U.S. citizenship to cast ballots in state elections. Officials insist the rule applies only to new sign-ups and state races, but this is plainly another tactic to shield entrenched power by erecting barriers that hit hardest on immigrants, working people, and communities of color. These groups already confront deep systemic obstacles rooted in historical exclusion and inequality when trying to secure the needed paperwork. Such institutional moves prioritize concentrating authority over expanding real democratic access for the vulnerable. We have to confront these restrictions directly and demand the structural reforms that actually deliver justice.
inputs.modified_text: In South Dakota, Governor Larry Rhoden signed Senate Bill 175 on Thursday, forcing new voter registrants to prove U.S. citizenship just to cast ballots in state elections. Even though officials claim this only targets fresh sign-ups and state races, it's another clear attempt by those in power to erect barriers that slam hardest into immigrants, working people, and communities of color. These groups already battle deep systemic obstacles tied to historical exclusion and inequality when trying to gather the required paperwork. Moves like this put concentrated authority ahead of any real expansion of democratic access for the vulnerable. We need to challenge these restrictions head-on and push for the structural reforms that can actually deliver justice.
